messages.author: 04b15f8a5125f402
messages.subject: R-INLA Man Page
parts:
Hello,

Is there a unix-style or CRAN-style man page somewhere? I've read a number of tutorials, and skimmed two books. I feel ready to begin working with INLA, but cannot find any complete summary of all functions and parameters. Does any such document exist?

If not, is there any effort to make such a document?

Thanks
Scott

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] R-INLA Man Page
parts:
I think its one of those things that is useful to have but no-one wants
to do ;-))

Additionally, not all documentation within the package is complete,
still some TODO's. And if anyone is keen to help us out, I'll happy to
merge it into the repo!

The recent book by Virgilio is good for general usage, and for spde
models, then the SPDE book is good. both are free to read online with
code.

Best
H

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] R-INLA Man Page
parts:
The package uses a somewhat hybrid documentation method for .Rd files, but the manual.pdf can be generated from those; it has nothing to do with CRAN.
Many of the .Rd files are nowadays generated via roxygen2, but some are generated by a bespoke system (since the package was started before roxygen2 was usable for this).
You can download/clone the github repository where all .Rd files are, and run devtools::build_manual().

But inla also has separate documentation for the latent models and priors, that live in separate, non-.Rd files (semi-automatically generated via latex, I think) that are normally opened via inla.doc(). Those aren't joined in a big document, but you could do that with a pdfjoin command or similar; should be possible in principle to auto-generate those documents to .Rd format as well, but it would take some effort; likely a bit easier to autogenerate a "models" document in RMarkdown format, but still would take effort to do.

Finn
